title: The Facilitator's review is a two-part test: alignment plus confirmed operational feasibility for GovOps
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3 adds a second requirement to the aligned-finding announcement: "In this Forum post, the Operational Facilitator must also confirm that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize."

Alignment and feasibility are distinct tests. The first asks whether the proposal is consistent with the Sky Core Atlas and the Osero Artifact; the second asks whether the people and systems responsible for execution can actually carry it out. A proposal can pass one and fail the other.

Binding them into a single announcement means holders never vote on something nobody can implement — the classic failure of governance systems where a passing vote produces an unexecutable mandate. It converts implementation capacity into an explicit precondition rather than a discovery made after the fact.

The trade-off is that feasibility is a judgment made by the same actor who screens alignment, and it is a softer criterion. "Not feasible for GovOps" is harder to contest than "misaligned with the Atlas," so the coupling that prevents unexecutable mandates also supplies a less falsifiable ground for declining a proposal.
description: An aligned proposal still fails if it cannot be operationalized; the Facilitator must publicly confirm both, coupling constitutional judgment to implementation capacity.
